<reason>A won by making comparable, passenger-facing service the success metric and converting CON’s matching/cost attack into a weighing dispute: concentrated exclusion versus modest shared delay. B’s idle-density critique stayed live and memorable, especially for ride-hail, but never showed those costs outweigh the harm or that absolute floors would close day-ahead gaps. A also answered pressure more directly, defining “close” and naming a rationing priority.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s Rebuttal 2 (A4.1–A4.5): substitution/coverage versus exclusive idle vans, an illustrative wait-gap, and concentrated exclusion versus modest edge cuts.</best_rebuttal>
